open_limitations: Constructed example; encoding diagnosis requires source metadata
Regex behavior depends on the stated engine and character policy
CSV dialect and missing-value rules must come from the provider
Whitespace tokens are not universal words; corpus is synthetic
Displayed catalog records come from a dated fixture; service behavior can change
Synthetic archived page tests selectors and cannot establish live-site coverage
OCR rates use one synthetic flyer and its deterministic degraded derivative; native engines can differ from the recorded 5.3.2 outputs
Reference labels encode one fictional codebook application and are not ground truth
Small keyword-model scores are not calibrated and have no external validity
Package fixtures demonstrate schemas and are not authenticated source subsets
Eleven fictional items cannot estimate reviewer reliability
Synthetic templates add no labor-market observations and still require human review
Rules were designed in-sample and challenge cases are not independent evaluation
Token counts describe this 28-sentence corpus only; a subword model trained on so little text is not representative
Coverage and out-of-vocabulary rates come from 28 sentences and estimate nothing about a larger collection
hunspell is a spelling dictionary with affix rules, not a universal morphological analyzer, and it ignores context
Held-out accuracy is measured on web text, so it does not transfer to job postings; per-token accuracy flatters a tagger
Attachment scores come from 13 weblog posts and do not transfer to job postings
Stem collisions and misses are counted on 28 sentences only
The two models are not a fair comparison; one was trained here on a tiny excerpt
Normalization choices are shown on a few strings and destroy information by design
A dictionary flags unknown words, not wrong ones; constructed errors are not a sample
Trigger words are not scope; the rule is scored on 28 hand-marked sentences
N-gram sparsity is demonstrated on 28 sentences and estimates nothing general
Hand-written patterns are scored against hand-marked sentences from one corpus
Chunk agreement is counted on 28 sentences with two models of unequal quality
A released model is applied to invented names; its errors show domain mismatch
Capitalised headings dominate the false positives in this particular corpus
Pay strings are constructed for teaching and are not a sample of real postings
The gazetteer is invented and deliberately contains one ambiguous place name
Resolution depends on a stated reference date; several expressions cannot resolve
Alias matching finds only what was written down; ambiguity is built into the data
The passage is constructed and the rule is a baseline, not a coreference system
All identifiers are invented; rule-based redaction is not safe for real personal data
Splitter scores come from one short constructed passage of hard cases
Paragraph rules depend on the file format and are shown on two formats only
Three rules are a demonstration; one is wrong by design to show why sound matters
Readability formulas count surface features and are not a reading level for a person
Threshold results come from a small constructed set of pairs
Every cleaning step is lossy; the examples are constructed to expose that
Metadata a document asserts about itself is not evidence; the fingerprint is
Two detectors trained on similar data can agree and still be wrong
Twenty-eight sentences cannot train a model; borrowing a larger corpus is a workaround, not a fix
Ten replicates of one corpus; the era signal may partly reflect period orthography rather than period content
Coefficients show what a linear model weighted, not whether a prediction is right
Deployment is shown without a running server, so nothing here tests real serving behaviour
Slices derived from the label make per-slice accuracy near-meaningless; drift cannot see a model confidently wrong
Nineteen test messages, all invented by the author; no number here describes real spam filtering
Lexicon coverage measured on formal prose does not transfer to short customer feedback
No performance number is reported because the author wrote both the messages and the classifier
One split of one corpus; the feature difference shown sits inside the replicate spread
Multi-label categories come from a hand-written dictionary, so agreement measures the dictionary
No ground truth for importance exists, so the comparison shows disagreement rather than quality
No reference summary exists for these speeches, so no summary quality claim is made
Topics are produced by a chosen k, not discovered; top-term tables invite over-reading
With 60 documents a trend can rest on one speech; vocabulary change and subject change are not separated
Outlier rank depends on the representation and on length; the top case is 135 words long
A 38-lemma slice of one WordNet release; sense inventories are curated and contested
Distance rankings depend on weighting and on document length
Similarity is defined by the representation, and speeches by one author dominate the nearest pairs
Trained on roughly 154,000 tokens, so neighbour lists look convincing while carrying little information
A small model's internal representation, not a large language model's, and not comparable across versions
